To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

transgenic mice expressing the human prion protein (hPrP) with P102L, E200K or M129V mutations and methionines at residue 129 (hPrP 102L/129M, 200K/129M or 129M/129V, respectively) are susceptible to prion disease after inoculation with human prions, but the incubation periods and the PrPSc properties of the disease vary according to the type of human prion strain

the human prion diseases with P102L and E200K mutations in PrP are efficiently transmitted to transgenic mice expressing the corresponding mutations in the human PrP, with disease incubation times similar to those of human patients with these mutations.

the P102L and E200K mutations in human prion protein (hPrP) are not sufficient to cause spontaneous disease in transgenic mice expressing these mutations and that the P102 L and E200 K mutations in hPrP have different effects on prion susceptibility in transgenic mice that depend on the prion strain type.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of animal models of human prion diseases, in which the human prion gene has been expressed in the context of the endogenous murine prion gene.
prion protein (PRNP) gene mutations and prion disease susceptibility.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of prion diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
human prion diseases associated with the P102L or the E200K mutations in the PrP gene can be transmitted to transgenic mice expressing the corresponding human PrP variants.

the human PrP 129 polymorphism is a significant determinant of prion susceptibility and the human PrP mutations have a differential influence on the susceptibility to classical and variant prion disease.
the PrP point mutation and the polymorphism at codon 129 have a significant impact on prion propagation, which is dependent on the prion strain type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the P102L and E200K mutations in human PrP have different effects on prion susceptibility that depend on the codon 127 genotype of the prion inoculum and host.

we show that transgenic mice expressing the human prion gene with pathogenic mutations are susceptible to infection with human prions and that the incubation period is influenced by the type of prion inoculated and by mismatch at residue 62.

the prion strains from patients carrying P102L or V180I PrP mutations were more pathogenic to mice expressing the mutant human prion protein, whereas the prion strains of patients carrying V180I or E200K PrP mutations were less pathogenic to mice with the same mutation in human prion protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prion strain is the most important determinant in determining the incubation period in these mice.
human PrP 129M, 102L transgenic mice are highly susceptible to P102L CJD prions and that the disease incubation period in these mice is shorter than that of classical CJD M, 102L mice.
transgenic mice expressing a human prion protein can be used as a model for prion diseases caused by pathogenic human prion protein mutations.
